## Description
<!-- Please describe the changes you made on a high level. -->
<!-- Make sure you reference the GitHub issue here if this change is related to one. -->
Instead of explicitly removing a key from the LruCache (which fails if the key class violates the equals() contract) call remove() on the iterator instead.

## Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!-- If it's fixing a bug reference it or provide repro steps. -->
Using this even cache keys violating equals() can be used here. Fixes #2532.

**Issue details / Repro steps / Use case background**: 
I have a RecyclerView full of LinearLayouts that contain largish ImageViews. They load asynchronously from the network. If I scroll fast enough after a while the app will crash.

**ModelLoader**:
```java
public class BGChartModelLoader extends BaseGlideUrlLoader<BGChart> {
    private final float mScale;

    protected BGChartModelLoader(ModelLoader<GlideUrl, InputStream> concreteLoader) {
        super(concreteLoader);

        final DisplayMetrics metrics = Resources.getSystem().getDisplayMetrics();
        mScale = metrics.density;
    }

    /**
     * The default factory for {@link }de.boersego.gmt.android.glide.BGChartModelLoader
     */
    public static class Factory implements ModelLoaderFactory<BGChart, InputStream> {

        @Override
        public ModelLoader<BGChart, InputStream> build(MultiModelLoaderFactory multiFactory) {
            return new BGChartModelLoader(multiFactory.build(GlideUrl.class, InputStream.class));
        }

        @Override
        public void teardown() {
        }
    }

    @Override
    protected String getUrl(final BGChart chart, final int width, final int height, final Options options) {
        final String locale = options.get(MyrGlideModule.OPTION_LOCALE);
        Float scaleOption = options.get(MyrGlideModule.OPTION_SCALE);
        final float scale = scaleOption != null ? scaleOption : mScale;

        return "http://charting.godmode-trader.de/t/app/config?id=" + chart.id + "&width=" + (width / mScale) + "&height=" + (height / mScale) + "&ratio=" + scale + "&_locale=" + locale;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean handles(BGChart o) {
        // We handle any Chart for now
        return true;
    }
}
```

comments: Sounds like your Model may not implement equals()/hashCode() correctly. Are they mutable?

This was indeed the case, equals had a bug. Thanks for the prompt reply and help!

Would the proposed change to trimToSize make sense in any case? It would reuse the existing iterator.
Sure I think that makes sense anyway, thanks for pointing it out.

Also thanks for the great amount of detail here, it's really helpful when trying to track this down. 

I may also be able to add an assertion somewhere in here that will at least throw with a better error message if we think the cache key has changed.

You're welcome - I guess using the bug report template is the least users can do ;)
Maybe the NULL returned by remove is good enough? Since in the iteration itself it shouldn't be possible to have a key that can't be removed.

@sjudd reopening as a reminder for the assertion

@unverbraucht well done on the report!

@unverbraucht Yeah that's what I was thinking initially. I think that would go away if you just use the iterator directly, though that's perfectly fine. I'll see if I can think of a more general way of detecting these changes. Let me know if you're interested in making the iterator change you suggested.
Can we have a release with this inside please? (PR #2550) 😃

review_comments: is there a chance of `ConcurrentModificationException` because of this line?

No, using the Iterator to remove is safe when using the Iterator itself to loop over the collection. I added another commit to ensure that we don't overrun the collection, although I don't see how it could happen unless the size to trim to is <0. Can't hurt though I guess.
@unverbraucht thoughts? I don't think we typically have concurrent modifications like this, but it's probably possible (and may be why the code was written the way it was initially).
@sjudd @TWiStErRob good point. It might make sense then to get a fresh instance of the Iterator after every loop run. I've committed proposed changes for that.
I agree in principle, but this matches the existing style, so let's just leave it as is for now.
